name: PaapiPlugin – Amazon Affiliate Product Boxes, Tables, Lists and Search
author: paapiplugin

sections.description:
PaapiPlugin puts Amazon product boxes and comparison tables on your WordPress site. Drop one product into a review, or line several up side by side in a buying guide. Every product link carries your Amazon Associate tag.

No credentials needed yet, free to start. Our Managed API returns live Amazon product data before you set up Amazon API credentials of your own. You get 20 searches and product lookups a day and 600 a month free, and your Amazon Associate tag always stays yours.

And your visitors can search too. Add [psfa_search] and visitors search, filter and browse Amazon’s catalog without leaving your page, so you also earn on products you never linked by hand.

Already approved for Amazon’s APIs? Bring your own Creators API (OAuth 2.0) or PA-API v5 credentials instead. Both paths live behind one toggle, so your site keeps earning through Amazon’s API transitions without rebuilding your pages.

What you can put on a page

  • Amazon product boxes (free) – one product inside a post, in a card, horizontal or minimal layout, with feature bullets and a title and star rating you can override. Build one from a keyword, Amazon link or ASIN with live preview.
  • Amazon comparison tables (free) – side-by-side buying-guide tables with image, title, rating, features and button columns.
  • Live Amazon product search (free) – visitors look for what they want and every result carries your tag.
  • Product grids (free) – a rotating Top Products grid on any page, or a fixed grid of products for one keyword.
  • Auto-updating lists (Premium) – a numbered top sellers or new releases list for a category that keeps itself current, refreshing at least once a day.

Product boxes, comparison tables and analytics ship inside the plugin.

Live demos and docs: https://paapiplugin.com/

Why Affiliates Use It

  • Show the products you recommend – a box inside a review or a table in a buying guide, each linking to Amazon with your tag
  • Earn on searches as well as your own picks – visitors find products you never had to curate
  • Loads only where you use it – the search scripts and styles load only on pages with a search or list shortcode, and the search box arrives pre-rendered with the page HTML
  • Smart caching – search results cached 30 min, product data cached 24 hr on the Managed API and 1 hr with your own credentials, so your API quota stays healthy

Free Features

  • Managed API – no Amazon API credentials needed yet; 20 searches and product lookups a day and 600 a month free, your Amazon Associate tag stays yours
  • Amazon marketplaces: all but Sweden on the Managed API; 11 marketplaces with your own credentials. Premium geotargeting sends visitors from other countries to their own Amazon store
  • Product boxes – [psfa_product_box asin="..."] in card, horizontal or minimal layout, with feature bullets and a title and star rating you can override
  • Comparison tables – [psfa_comparison id="..."] with image, title, rating, features and button columns in a horizontal layout
  • Live Amazon product search with autocomplete suggestions
  • Top Products Grid – with no query or category set, [psfa_search] shows a rotating grid of popular Amazon products across categories instead of an empty search box
  • Keyword product grids – show a fixed set of products for one search term, with no search box or pagination, for example [psfa_search query="standing desk" count="4" pagination="none" hide_search="true"]
  • Brand, price range, condition, merchant, and availability filters (Price Range, Condition, Merchant, and In-Stock apply when you bring your own Amazon credentials; see the Managed API FAQ)
  • Sorting: Relevance and Customer Reviews everywhere; price sorting, Newest Arrivals, and Featured apply when you bring your own Amazon credentials
  • Responsive, mobile-first grid layout
  • 5 categories (Electronics, Books, Fashion, Toys & Games, Home & Garden)
  • Up to 50 products (5 pages) with infinite scroll, Load More, or no pagination
  • Customizable product count (2-20 per page)
  • Hide the category banner, search bar, or filters
  • Visual shortcode builder – no coding required
  • Cache management page with usage monitoring
  • One fixed theme preset: Neutral base color, Orange accent, Vega card style, 0.5 border radius, System Default font, light mode
  • CSS classes on titles, brands, prices and deal badges for custom CSS

Premium Features

  • Every Amazon category your store offers – the full department list for your marketplace
  • Extended pagination – up to Amazon’s 10-page ceiling (up to 100 products) on any connection; on the Managed API a filtered search stops at 3 pages
  • List layout – vertical display for detailed product comparisons
  • Full appearance control – 5 base colors, 17 accent colors, 5 card styles, 5 border radius levels, dark mode, 16 fonts
  • Winner badges – mark a pick such as Best Value or Editor’s Choice on product boxes and comparison tables
  • Product box styles – Editorial and Spotlight, for every layout
  • Button text color – Auto, White or Dark text on buttons and badges
  • Product text – color and size for titles, brands, prices and deal badges
  • Table sizes and layouts – size options, a vertical layout and a stacked mobile mode for comparison tables
  • Auto-updating lists – [psfa_list type="bestsellers"] or [psfa_list type="new"] shows a numbered list of products for a category, refreshed at least once a day. With your own Amazon credentials, top sellers are a keyword and category search ordered by Amazon sales rank. On the Managed API, top sellers come from Amazon’s own Best Sellers list for the category, with no keyword needed. Build one on the Lists page
  • Geotargeting – add a tracking ID for each Amazon store you have joined, and visitors from those countries go to their own store when they open a product link. It uses the visitor’s browser time zone instead of an IP lookup or cookie, and it works behind page caches on either connection.
  • Deal badges – Lightning Deal, Best Deal, Prime Exclusive, Low Stock warning, discount percentage, deal countdown timer (with your own Amazon credentials)
  • Product badges – Best Seller rank (#1-100)
  • Deals filters – let visitors narrow to products with active deals or a minimum discount (with your own Amazon credentials)
  • Analytics – track searches, clicks, impressions, and filter usage, including on product boxes and tables. Dashboard with charts, date picker, CSV/JSON export. Privacy-first, no cookies or PII
  • White-label mode – remove all PaapiPlugin branding
  • Button and display customization – buy button color and size, custom button text, hide Amazon icon
  • Settings import and export – copy settings between sites, also with WP-CLI
  • More Managed API capacity – 1,200 searches and product lookups a month per site (Agency: 3,600 shared across all your sites)

Plans and prices: https://paapiplugin.com/pricing/

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Choose how to connect: turn on our Managed API to start showing products with no credentials needed yet, or enter your own Creators API or PA-API v5 credentials
  3. Add a product box, a comparison table or the search to any page or post (in the block editor, use a Shortcode block): [psfa_product_box asin="..."], [psfa_comparison id="..."] or [psfa_search]
  4. Visitors click through to Amazon with your Associate tag on the link, and you earn commission on what they buy

Requirements

  • WordPress 5.8 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • cURL extension enabled
  • An Amazon Associates account. For product data, use our Managed API (no credentials needed yet) or bring your own Creators API or PA-API v5 credentials (Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and Associate Tag)

Privacy & Security

  • Your own Amazon API secret keys are stored encrypted, and once saved they never reach the browser
  • On the Managed API, calls are server-to-server from your WordPress site to our proxy, which returns live Amazon product data tagged with your Associate ID. We never receive your site visitors’ IP addresses or personal data
  • The Managed API uses a third-party Amazon product-data provider on the back end. Full detail is in our Privacy Policy and Managed API Usage Terms at paapiplugin.com
  • The optional product-update email opt-in is the only marketing data we collect, and only if you check the box. It never affects your API key or service
  • All requests use secure HTTPS connections

Support

For support, feature requests, or bug reports, please visit the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org.

Credits

This plugin uses the Amazon Creators API (recommended) and the Amazon Product Advertising API 5.0 (PA-API 5.0) to search and retrieve product information. A Managed API option is also available, which connects through PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy.

Third-Party Libraries

This plugin includes the following open-source libraries:

  • shadcn/ui – UI component library (MIT License)
  • Radix UI – Accessible UI primitives used by shadcn/ui (MIT License)
  • Lucide React – Icon library (ISC License)
  • Phosphor Icons – Duotone icon set, used for select inline SVG icons (MIT License)
  • React – UI framework (MIT License)
  • Tailwind CSS – Utility-first CSS framework (MIT License)

Source Code

The JavaScript bundles are built from TypeScript and React source files using the tools listed below.

Build tools used:
* Vite – For TypeScript/React bundling and minification
* Node.js – Runtime environment
* React 19 – Admin UI and frontend rendering
* Tailwind CSS v4 – Utility-first styling
* shadcn/ui – Accessible UI components built on Radix UI primitives
* Lucide React – Icon library used by UI components
* Phosphor Icons – Duotone icon set (inline SVGs)

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

Amazon Product APIs (Creators API and PA-API 5.0)

This plugin uses Amazon’s Creators API (OAuth 2.0, recommended) or Product Advertising API (PA-API 5.0, legacy) to search and retrieve product information when you bring your own Amazon credentials. This is the core functionality of the plugin.

  • What it does: Searches Amazon’s product catalog and retrieves product details (title, price, images, etc.)
  • When data is sent: When a user performs a product search on your website
  • What data is sent: Search queries, category selections, and filter parameters
  • Service provider: Amazon.com, Inc.
  • Terms of Service: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/agreement
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=468496

PaapiPlugin Managed API

If you enable the optional Managed API, this plugin sends search requests to PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy, which retrieves live Amazon product data on your behalf through a third-party Amazon product-data provider. You do not need your own Amazon API credentials on this path.

  • What it does: Returns live Amazon product search, product detail and Best Sellers list data without requiring your own Amazon API credentials
  • When data is sent: When a visitor performs a product search on your website, and when an auto-updating list refreshes itself in the background (sent server-to-server from your WordPress site)
  • What data is sent: Search keywords, ASINs, filter parameters, category or sub-category number, your Amazon Associate tag, your WordPress site URL, and your WordPress server IP address. End-visitor IP addresses and personal data are not sent.
  • Service provider: PaapiPlugin (uses a third-party Amazon product-data provider on the back end)
  • Terms of Service: https://paapiplugin.com/api-terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://paapiplugin.com/privacy-policy/

PaapiPlugin Admin Messages

If your site is connected to the PaapiPlugin Managed API, or you opted in to Freemius usage tracking, this plugin fetches a short list of plain-text messages (product news and offers) from PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy and shows them in the notification bell on the plugin’s own admin pages. Sites that use neither never make this request.

  • What it does: Retrieves a short list of plain-text messages for the plugin’s admin notification bell. The plugin chooses which messages to show on your own server, by plan, plugin version and dates. Each message is text with at most one link, to paapiplugin.com or wordpress.org. No code is ever sent.
  • When data is sent: About once a day, server-to-server from your WordPress site, and only if the site is connected to the Managed API or opted in to Freemius usage tracking. If a fetch fails, the plugin tries again an hour later.
  • What data is sent: No site data. The request does not include your site URL, your Amazon Associate tag, any email address or any search terms. As with any web request, the service sees your WordPress server IP address. Our proxy does not save anything from this request.
  • Service provider: PaapiPlugin
  • Service URL: https://paapiplugin-api-proxy.ith3nate.workers.dev/v1/notices
  • Terms of Service: https://paapiplugin.com/terms-and-conditions/
  • Privacy Policy: https://paapiplugin.com/privacy-policy/

Amazon Autocomplete Suggestions

This plugin uses Amazon’s autocomplete API to provide search suggestions as users type.

  • What it does: Provides real-time search suggestions based on user input
  • When data is sent: When a user types in the search box (after 2+ characters)
  • What data is sent: The partial search query text
  • Service provider: Amazon.com, Inc.
  • Service URL: https://completion.amazon.com/
  • Terms of Service: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=468496

Google Fonts (Premium Feature)

Premium users can select custom fonts from Google Fonts for product display elements.

  • What it does: Loads custom font files for typography customization
  • When data is sent: When a page with the product search is loaded and custom fonts are configured
  • What data is sent: Font family names
  • Service provider: Google LLC
  • Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Privacy Policy

How product data is retrieved depends on the connection path you choose. When you bring your own credentials, product searches use your Amazon API credentials and product data comes from Amazon’s Creators API or PA-API. On the Managed API, search requests go to PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy, which retrieves product data through a third-party Amazon product-data provider rather than Amazon’s official Creators API or PA-API. On that path we receive search keywords, your Amazon Associate tag, your WordPress site URL, your WordPress server IP address, and the Amazon category or sub-category number of an auto-updating list, when your site refreshes one, as listed in the External Services section above. Separately, sites connected to the Managed API or opted in to Freemius usage tracking fetch a short list of plain-text admin messages from PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy about once a day; that request carries no site data, as described under PaapiPlugin Admin Messages in the External Services section above. We never collect, store, or transmit your site visitors’ personal data on either path. Please refer to the External Services section above for details on third-party services used by this plugin.
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New in your WordPress admin.
  2. Search for “PaapiPlugin – Amazon Affiliate Product Boxes, Tables, Lists and Search” (or upload the ZIP from WordPress.org once approved).
  3. Click Install Now and then Activate.

Manual Installation

  1. Upload the paapi-product-search-for-amazon folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to PaapiPlugin in your WordPress admin sidebar.
  4. Under Settings → Amazon connection, enter your Amazon API credentials (Creators API recommended, or PA-API v5), or enable the Managed API for no-credential setup.
  5. Add the shortcode [psfa_search] to any page or post.

Premium Installation

Premium is a separate ZIP that you download from your account dashboard at paapiplugin.com after purchase. It is a full replacement for the free plugin, not an add-on, so only one copy of the plugin should ever be installed on a site.

  1. In Plugins → Installed Plugins, click Deactivate on the free version of PaapiPlugin.
  2. Click Delete on the now-deactivated free plugin. Your settings and API credentials are kept: the plugin stores them in the WordPress database and removes nothing when you delete it, so the premium version picks them up on activation.
  3. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose the premium ZIP you downloaded, and click Install Now.
  4. Click Activate Plugin.
  5. Activate your license when the plugin prompts you after activation. If you are not prompted, open PaapiPlugin in your WordPress admin sidebar and click Activate License.

Uploading the premium ZIP through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin is safe on its own. WordPress replaces the existing plugin folder in place, so you never end up with two copies.

Do not leave a second copy of the plugin in a differently named folder. If you unzip the premium build by hand, or upload it over FTP into a folder such as /wp-content/plugins/paapi-product-search-for-amazon-pro/ while the original /wp-content/plugins/paapi-product-search-for-amazon/ is still there, WordPress sees two copies of the same plugin. Activating the second one while the first is active produces:

Plugin could not be activated because it triggered a fatal error.

The fix is the sequence above: deactivate the free version, delete it, then install the premium ZIP.

Configuration

  1. Open PaapiPlugin in your WordPress admin sidebar, then Settings → Amazon connection.
  2. Select your Authentication Type:
    • OAuth 2.0 (Creators API) – Recommended for new users
    • AWS Signature V4 (PA-API) – Legacy authentication method
  3. For OAuth 2.0 (Creators API):
    • Enter your Client ID and Client Secret from Creators API
    • Enter your Credential Version (typically “1”)
    • Select your Auth Region and Marketplace
  4. For AWS Signature V4 (PA-API):
    • Enter your Access Key ID and Secret Access Key
  5. Enter your Associate Tag (your Amazon Associates ID).
  6. Click Test Connection to verify your credentials work.
  7. Click Save Settings.
  8. (Optional) Customize appearance on the Appearance page (base color, accent, button text color, product text, buy button, radius, dark mode, font).
sections.faq:
How is this different from other Amazon affiliate plugins?

Most Amazon affiliate plugins display products you already picked: you find the ASIN, embed it, and that is what your reader sees. PaapiPlugin does that too: product boxes, comparison tables and product grids are built in and free to start. On top of that it puts live Amazon search on your page, so readers can find products you never linked, and every result still carries your Associate tag. Run it next to the plugin you use now, or use it in its place.

Do I need Amazon API credentials to use this plugin?

No. Our Managed API runs live Amazon product search with no Amazon API credentials needed yet and no AWS keys. You still need a free Amazon Associates account so commissions are tagged to you, and your Amazon Associate tag is always yours. If you already hold Creators API or PA-API v5 credentials, you can bring your own instead with one toggle in the plugin admin.

Do I need an Amazon Associates account?

Yes, a free Amazon Associates account is always required so commissions are tagged to you. For product data you can use our Managed API (no credentials needed yet) or your own Creators API (or legacy PA-API v5) credentials. Either way, your Associate Tag tags every product link with your affiliate ID.

How do I get Amazon API credentials?

  1. Sign up for Amazon Associates
  2. Apply for Creators API (recommended) or PA-API v5 access
  3. Enter your credentials under Settings → Amazon connection in the plugin and click Test Connection

Will this slow down my site?

The search scripts and styles load only on pages that include the [psfa_search] or [psfa_list] shortcode, so your other pages don’t load them. On a search page, the search box is pre-rendered at build time and arrives with the page HTML, so it shows up without waiting for JavaScript; the product results are then drawn in the browser. Search results are cached for 30 minutes. Product data is cached for 24 hours on the Managed API and 1 hour with your own Amazon credentials. Products in boxes and tables refresh once a day, and each refresh is one lookup, so the free plan covers about 20 products. A repeated search is answered from your site’s cache instead of a new Amazon request, which also keeps your API quota healthy.

What’s included in the free version?

The free version is a real product, not a crippled trial. You get product boxes (card, horizontal and minimal layouts in the Classic style) and comparison tables (image, title, rating, features and button columns) on the Managed API within the free quota, plus live Amazon search with autocomplete, 5 categories, 50 products, brand/price/condition filters (price and condition filters apply when you bring your own Amazon credentials), sorting, infinite scroll, caching, responsive grid layout, and a visual shortcode builder. Premium adds every category your Amazon store offers, 100 products, the Editorial and Spotlight product box styles, auto-updating lists, geotargeting, deal badges (with your own Amazon credentials), full appearance customization, list layout, and white-label mode.

Can visitors see products without searching first?

Yes. With no query and no category set, [psfa_search] shows the Top Products Grid: a rotating grid of popular Amazon products across categories instead of an empty search box, so any page becomes a ready-made Amazon storefront. This is the Top Products on Empty State setting, on by default. To force the grid on when that setting is off, use [psfa_search mode=”top”]. If you set a category, it shows popular products from that category instead. Either way, visitors can search or filter from there and every product link carries your Amazon Associate tag.

Are Amazon product boxes and comparison tables included in the free version?

Yes. Product boxes and comparison tables are built in and free to start, alongside live search, the Top Products grid and keyword product grids. Premium adds winner badges, the Editorial and Spotlight product box styles, more table sizes and layouts, auto-updating lists, geotargeting, and deal badges when you bring your own Amazon credentials. The Free and Premium lists in the Description show the full split.

Is there a Gutenberg block?

PaapiPlugin does not have a block of its own. It uses shortcodes, and the block editor runs them through its built-in Shortcode block: add a Shortcode block and paste [psfa_search], the [psfa_product_box] or [psfa_comparison] shortcode for a product box or comparison table, or [psfa_list] for an auto-updating list. The Search page under Create in the plugin admin writes the search shortcode for you. The same shortcodes work in the Classic editor too.

Does it work with Elementor and other page builders?

Yes, through the builder’s own shortcode element (in Elementor, that is the Shortcode widget). There is no dedicated Elementor widget. The plugin loads its scripts and styles when the shortcode renders, so the search works even when a builder keeps the page layout outside the normal post content.

Can I customize how it looks on my site?

Yes. Free users get the Neutral base with orange accent. Premium users pick the base color (5 options), accent color (17 options), button text color, card style (5 presets), border radius, dark mode and font (15 Google Fonts + system default), and can set the color and size of product titles, brands, prices, deal badges and the buy button. Product boxes also come in three styles: Classic for everyone, plus Editorial and Spotlight with Premium. On every plan, titles, brands, prices and deal badges have their own CSS classes (psfa-el-title, psfa-el-brand, psfa-el-price, psfa-el-deal) if you prefer custom CSS.

Does it work with caching plugins?

Yes, but you may need to exclude pages with the [psfa_search] shortcode from full-page caching, since the search functionality requires dynamic content.

Can I use it on multiple sites?

Yes. Each site needs its own license and Amazon API credentials.

What happens if Amazon changes or retires the PA-API?

We recommend the Creators API (OAuth 2.0), Amazon’s current product API, or our Managed API, which needs no credentials yet. PA-API v5 (AWS Signature V4) is Amazon’s older method; if you still have working PA-API credentials the plugin continues to support them. You can switch between any of these in the plugin admin without rebuilding your pages, so your site keeps earning through Amazon’s API transitions.

Do I need to manually maintain product lists or hunt for ASINs?

No. That is the point of search. Visitors type what they want and see live Amazon results filtered by brand, price, and condition. You never need to pick ASINs or keep a product list updated. Every click still carries your Associate tag, so you earn on whatever they decide to buy. If you want a ready-made list on the page, paid plans add auto-updating lists ([psfa_list]): a top sellers or new releases list for a category that rebuilds itself and refreshes at least once a day.

Why don’t I see the Condition, Merchant, and In-Stock filters on the Managed API?

On the Managed API path, the managed search data does not include per-item condition (new/used/refurbished), seller/merchant, or stock-availability detail, so the Condition, Merchant, and In-Stock filters would have no effect. To avoid showing controls that do nothing, they are hidden automatically when you use the Managed API. These filters remain available when you connect your own Amazon credentials (Creators API or PA-API v5), where Amazon provides that data.

Why don’t I see the Newest Arrivals and Featured sort options on the Managed API?

On the Managed API path, the search sort menu leaves out Newest Arrivals and Featured (Featured would match the default Relevance order there). For the newest products, use an auto-updating new releases list instead: [psfa_list type="new"] works on the Managed API on every paid plan and shows a keyword and category search sorted newest first. In a few departments Amazon ignores newest-first sorting, and the list then shows Amazon’s usual order. Both sort options remain available in search when you connect your own Amazon credentials (Creators API or PA-API v5). The Customer Reviews sort remains available on the Managed API and is applied by Amazon’s own search when results are fetched.

  • New: While PaapiPlugin is connected and no published post or page holds its shortcode, a notice on the WordPress Dashboard and the Posts and Pages lists shows the next step. Dismiss it once to hide it for two weeks, twice to hide it for good.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Choose how to connect: turn on our Managed API to start showing products with no credentials needed yet, or enter your own Creators API or PA-API v5 credentials
  3. Add a product box, a comparison table or the search to any page or post (in the block editor, use a Shortcode block): [psfa_product_box asin="..."], [psfa_comparison id="..."] or [psfa_search]
  4. Visitors click through to Amazon with your Associate tag on the link, and you earn commission on what they buy

Requirements

  • WordPress 5.8 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • cURL extension enabled
  • An Amazon Associates account. For product data, use our Managed API (no credentials needed yet) or bring your own Creators API or PA-API v5 credentials (Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and Associate Tag)

Privacy & Security

  • Your own Amazon API secret keys are stored encrypted, and once saved they never reach the browser
  • On the Managed API, calls are server-to-server from your WordPress site to our proxy, which returns live Amazon product data tagged with your Associate ID. We never receive your site visitors’ IP addresses or personal data
  • The Managed API uses a third-party Amazon product-data provider on the back end. Full detail is in our Privacy Policy and Managed API Usage Terms at paapiplugin.com
  • The optional product-update email opt-in is the only marketing data we collect, and only if you check the box. It never affects your API key or service
  • All requests use secure HTTPS connections

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

Amazon Product APIs (Creators API and PA-API 5.0)

This plugin uses Amazon’s Creators API (OAuth 2.0, recommended) or Product Advertising API (PA-API 5.0, legacy) to search and retrieve product information when you bring your own Amazon credentials. This is the core functionality of the plugin.

  • What it does: Searches Amazon’s product catalog and retrieves product details (title, price, images, etc.)
  • When data is sent: When a user performs a product search on your website
  • What data is sent: Search queries, category selections, and filter parameters
  • Service provider: Amazon.com, Inc.
  • Terms of Service: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/agreement
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=468496

PaapiPlugin Managed API

If you enable the optional Managed API, this plugin sends search requests to PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy, which retrieves live Amazon product data on your behalf through a third-party Amazon product-data provider. You do not need your own Amazon API credentials on this path.

  • What it does: Returns live Amazon product search, product detail and Best Sellers list data without requiring your own Amazon API credentials
  • When data is sent: When a visitor performs a product search on your website, and when an auto-updating list refreshes itself in the background (sent server-to-server from your WordPress site)
  • What data is sent: Search keywords, ASINs, filter parameters, category or sub-category number, your Amazon Associate tag, your WordPress site URL, and your WordPress server IP address. End-visitor IP addresses and personal data are not sent.
  • Service provider: PaapiPlugin (uses a third-party Amazon product-data provider on the back end)
  • Terms of Service: https://paapiplugin.com/api-terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://paapiplugin.com/privacy-policy/

PaapiPlugin Admin Messages

If your site is connected to the PaapiPlugin Managed API, or you opted in to Freemius usage tracking, this plugin fetches a short list of plain-text messages (product news and offers) from PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy and shows them in the notification bell on the plugin’s own admin pages. Sites that use neither never make this request.

  • What it does: Retrieves a short list of plain-text messages for the plugin’s admin notification bell. The plugin chooses which messages to show on your own server, by plan, plugin version and dates. Each message is text with at most one link, to paapiplugin.com or wordpress.org. No code is ever sent.
  • When data is sent: About once a day, server-to-server from your WordPress site, and only if the site is connected to the Managed API or opted in to Freemius usage tracking. If a fetch fails, the plugin tries again an hour later.
  • What data is sent: No site data. The request does not include your site URL, your Amazon Associate tag, any email address or any search terms. As with any web request, the service sees your WordPress server IP address. Our proxy does not save anything from this request.
  • Service provider: PaapiPlugin
  • Service URL: https://paapiplugin-api-proxy.ith3nate.workers.dev/v1/notices
  • Terms of Service: https://paapiplugin.com/terms-and-conditions/
  • Privacy Policy: https://paapiplugin.com/privacy-policy/

Amazon Autocomplete Suggestions

This plugin uses Amazon’s autocomplete API to provide search suggestions as users type.

  • What it does: Provides real-time search suggestions based on user input
  • When data is sent: When a user types in the search box (after 2+ characters)
  • What data is sent: The partial search query text
  • Service provider: Amazon.com, Inc.
  • Service URL: https://completion.amazon.com/
  • Terms of Service: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=468496

Google Fonts (Premium Feature)

Premium users can select custom fonts from Google Fonts for product display elements.

  • What it does: Loads custom font files for typography customization
  • When data is sent: When a page with the product search is loaded and custom fonts are configured
  • What data is sent: Font family names
  • Service provider: Google LLC
  • Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Privacy Policy

How product data is retrieved depends on the connection path you choose. When you bring your own credentials, product searches use your Amazon API credentials and product data comes from Amazon’s Creators API or PA-API. On the Managed API, search requests go to PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy, which retrieves product data through a third-party Amazon product-data provider rather than Amazon’s official Creators API or PA-API. On that path we receive search keywords, your Amazon Associate tag, your WordPress site URL, your WordPress server IP address, and the Amazon category or sub-category number of an auto-updating list, when your site refreshes one, as listed in the External Services section above. Separately, sites connected to the Managed API or opted in to Freemius usage tracking fetch a short list of plain-text admin messages from PaapiPlugin’s hosted proxy about once a day; that request carries no site data, as described under PaapiPlugin Admin Messages in the External Services section above. We never collect, store, or transmit your site visitors’ personal data on either path. Please refer to the External Services section above for details on third-party services used by this plugin.
